questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this login flow authenticates customers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the service run bcrypt.compare against DUMMY_HASH when no customer matches the email?
choices: To make the unknown-email response take about as long as a wrong-password response, so timing does not reveal which emails are registered
To warm up the bcrypt worker pool for the next request
To increment a global failed-attempt counter
To verify that the bcrypt library is configured with cost 12

questions.prompt: Two wrong-password requests for the same customer arrive at the same moment, when failed_attempts is 3. What does incrementFailedAttempts return to each?
choices: Both get 4, because each read the old value before writing
One gets 4 and the other 5, because the increment is a single atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING
Both get 5, because Postgres merges the two updates
One fails with a serialization error

questions.prompt: A customer types 'Alice@Shop.com ' when the stored email is 'alice@shop.com'. What happens?
choices: 400 because the email has trailing whitespace
Login proceeds normally because the email is trimmed and lowercased before lookup
423 because of the mismatch counts as a failed attempt
